>look
Holmes's Study
 
The study is in its usual disarray.
 
Your friend is slouched on the sofa, lost in a black mood of despair. He is pale and emaciated, and his sharp eyes burn with fever. He is staring at a phial that he holds in one hand. His free hand rests near a hypodermic syringe in a neat morocco case at his side. You realize that he is fighting a depression brought on by what he calls "the dull routine of existence."
 
The bedroom door to the west is closed. The only other exit is the door to the south.
 
You see a pigeon, a violin and a newspaper. You see a morocco case on the sofa. Holmes is here. You see a pipe, a persian slipper, a knife, some mail and a pistol on the mantelpiece.
